# ListenerDoppler <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [3D Sound](Blitz3D-3D-Sound)

</div>


```blitzbasic
ListenerDoppler:Void value:Float32, fade_ms:Int32=0
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | In | Float32 | required | `0` turns the shift off, `1` is the real one and `2` shifts twice as far. Below 0 is a runtime error. |
| `fade_ms` | In | Int32 | `0` | How many milliseconds it takes to get to the new value. `0` (the default) changes it at once. Below 0 is a runtime error. |

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Changes how strong the pitch shift of moving 3D sounds is, which [CreateListener](CreateListener) sets first. A game that leaves a planet for space can turn the shift down as the air goes, without a new listener. This is a BlitzLLVM extension.

## Differences

* [ChannelDoppler](ChannelDoppler) scales it for one channel on top. [GetListenerDoppler](GetListenerDoppler) tells the value.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
; Leaving the atmosphere: no doppler shift after five seconds.
ListenerDoppler 0, 5000
```
